panels.title: Shop reachable (LAN probe)
panels.description: **1 = shop answered a ping from pascal within the last minute, 0 = it did not.** The probe writes `shop_health` once per minute with no smoothing, so a single failed ping shows as one minute of 0. Ignore isolated single-point dips; a sustained 0 is an outage. When the line disappears entirely the probe itself (pascal or the node_exporter textfile collector) is down. Metric: `shop_health{mode="lan"}` from `monitor/shop-health.sh`.

panels.title: Node scrape status
panels.description: **1 = VictoriaMetrics scrapes the node_exporter successfully.** One line per Pi. `shop:9100` is the shop Pi itself, `pascal:9100` is the witness host that runs the probe. `up=0` for shop means we have no data from the machine at all and must rely on the LAN probe.

panels.title: Probe freshness
panels.description: **Seconds since pascal last recorded a probe result.** Normally a sawtooth between 0 and ~60 s. If this keeps growing, the probe pipeline (systemd timer, script, textfile dir on pascal) is broken and `shop_health` can no longer be trusted - `shop_health` would freeze at its last value while the freshness gauge keeps climbing.

panels.title: Reachability over 30 days
panels.description: Known outages of shop in the last month (UTC): **09-02 14:15 -> 20:00 (5.8 h)**, **09-04 20:50 -> 09-09 13:40 (4.7 d)**, **09-10 22:30 -> 09-18 07:30 (7.4 d)** - root cause analysis in the `shop` repo README. Since the observer roles were deployed on 09-18 you should see this line go solid: the LAN probe (`shop_health`) only exists from 09-18 onward, `up` for `pascal:9100` starts the same day. Any new `0` below the pascal line rules out WiFi/mains as the cause; pascal staying up while shop drops points at shop itself.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: How long shop has been up. **A reset of this line is a reboot** - check the journal for the cause. A reboot while the LAN probe stays green is suspicious: the wifi stack recovered by itself (or something rebooted the box).

panels.title: CPU load
panels.description: 1m and 5m load average. Load > 1 sustained on this Pi means something is grinding; correlates with the camera/mediamtx work.

panels.title: Memory available
panels.description: Free memory as seen by the kernel. A step towards zero can precede an OOM kill of a service (e.g. the camera pipeline).

panels.title: Root filesystem free
panels.description: Free space on the SD card (`/dev/mmcblk0p2`, `mountpoint="/"`). The 2024 incident was a read-only SD card; a slow grind towards zero is the warning sign. log2ram keeps `/var/log` off the card.

panels.title: SoC temperature
panels.description: CPU thermal zone. The Pi throttles at 80+ C; the watchdog role warns about undervoltage/throttling from `vcgencmd get_throttled` (not yet exported as a metric - see README).

panels.title: Uptime (pascal)
panels.description: pascal sits on the same WiFi and mains as shop and runs the LAN probe. **Its uptime is the control variable**: pascal up while shop is down rules out WiFi and mains as the cause of a shop outage (this is what proved the 09-11 incident was shop-internal).

panels.title: CPU load (pascal)
panels.description: pascal is the 3D printer server; typically idle. Spikes here are unrelated to shop but can delay the probe execution.

panels.title: Plugs reachable (gosund-0..2)
panels.description: Tasmota power plugs on the house LAN (192.168.1.10-.12, same network as shop and pascal). **When the mains cut on 09-17 -> 09-18, these dropped together with both Pis.** They double as a power-loss detector and can later remote-cycle the Pi's PSU.

panels.title: Mains voltage (gosund-0..2)
panels.description: Mains voltage measured by the plugs (nominal 230 V). Sagging mains is the suspected root cause of shop's brownout-induced WiFi/SD flakiness (PSU under-voltage, `get_throttled=0x50000` on 09-18). Watch for drops correlated with workshop load.
